title: The fee accrual has no home in rwb-litigation and no named operation on rwb-payment
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-011, story and data table); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.11; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T3.1 and T-A.1; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-41 to R-LIT-43; _work/msr/context/S4.md (service row and ownership rows)
section: RWB-S4-E5011-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 (AC1), 8 (BR5), 11, 12.2, 12.8, 13, 19; RWB-S4-E5011-CON sections 1, 2, 3, 7 (AC3), 8 (BR5), 11, 12.2, 12.8, 19; the metadata rows and the two fragments
description: The legacy story says the step 'accrues the fees against the case', and R-LIT-42 posts the fee against the case. No part of rwb-litigation can hold or post it: the ownership rows of the service name only hearing and legal_action as its tables, neither of which carries a fee, a spend, an amount or a posting column in TSD S4 T3.1, and no fee table exists in the schema. The fee therefore belongs to P8 rwb-payment, whose module is 'Payments and posting' (context pack slide 4), but rwb-payment appears in no dependency row of this key, in no metadata row and in no ownership row of S4, and no source read for this key names a payment operation, a field list or a spend limit. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the step needs only its own contract and the two platform contracts.
evidence: Context pack: 'Tables (2) hearing, legal_action'; 'REST operations provided (5)'; 'Events (0)'; 'Jobs (0)'; 'Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow'. TSD S4 T3.1 gives legal_action 14 fields (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing 6 (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029), none of them a fee or a posting; T-A.1 gives five operations and none of them touches money. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: R-LIT-41 'Route the fee to the approver inside the D7.4 limit', R-LIT-42 'Raise the fee and post it against the case', systems 'ALS core and GL'. FSD S4 A2.11.3.1 carries only VR-S4-011-1 and BR-S4-011. The metadata rows of both stories carry Contract, Integration and External dependencies None.
area: Application and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P8 rwb-payment
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P8 rwb-payment architect and the business owner of S4
proposed: Keep the legacy sentence unchanged with its origin tag and record the target reading: the accrued fee, its spend deadline, its value date and its approval state are read on rwb-payment's contract (one hop, 2 s, faked, operation name left as the placeholder); this service records the spend decision of R-LIT-41 to R-LIT-43 through its decision record and raises the approved fact, and posts nothing; rwb-payment appears on the contract rows of both stories and the metadata rows stay as the plan gives them.

title: The deadline has no value in any source and its row belongs to rwb-case, while the service owns no Schedule or job
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-011 data table: timer, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-33, R-LIT-34, R-LIT-35 (timer column 'To the hearing date', 'To the new date'); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T4, T5.3; _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows: Jobs 0, Workflows 1; Temporal slides 5 and 7)
section: RWB-S4-E5011-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 4 (steps 7 to 9), 5 (X8), 7 (AC1), 8 (BR2), 9, 11, 12.5, 12.6, 13, 19; RWB-S4-E5011-CON sections 2, 3, 7 (AC6), 8 (BR7), 11, 12.5, 12.6, 12.9, 19; the workflows keys of both fragments
description: Two values and one home are missing. (1) The value: no source gives the hearing lead time, the escalation horizon or any working-day rule for a hearing deadline; the rules say only 'To the hearing date' and 'To the new date', and R-LIT-33 to R-LIT-35 carry no number. (2) The home: the legacy data table names the `timer` row (DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036) as the clock, but that row is rwb-case's projection and not a litigation table, and this service owns no Job and no Schedule. (3) The surface: the timer appears in no ownership row of S4 and the workflow kit contract is in no dependency row, although `LitigationWorkflow` is the declared host of the clock.
evidence: Context pack: 'Jobs (0) - None', 'Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow'. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-33 ('Schedule the hearing and set the deadline timer', timer 'To the hearing date'), R-LIT-34 ('Reset the hearing timer and record the postpone reason code'), R-LIT-35 ('Return the case to the hearing calendar'). TSD S4 T4 lists the states and no timer value; T5.3 says 'Events - None'. Legacy data table: 'timer | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at and 4 more | DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036'. Context pack slide 7 notes: 'Temporal timer fires the warning automatically; Drools escalates when 90 days or less remain'; slide 5 notes the DEV rule set pauses the stage clock and never the prescription clock.
area: Workflow and timer design, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case architect and the Temporal platform owner
proposed: Read each deadline as a durable timer of `LitigationWorkflow` on queue rwb-litigation: the sitting date from `hearing_date` and the re-armed date from `next_date`, with the reference values (lead time, escalation horizon) as versioned rows carried by the placeholder. Write no `timer` row, declare no Schedule and no Quartz row, and name the workflow kit as a contract dependency in the contract story only, leaving the metadata rows as the plan gives them.

title: The rule package read and the reference values carry no dependency row, and DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07 are outside the pattern set
source: _work/msr/context/S4.md (Decoupling patterns short table; ownership rows: Events 0, Jobs 0); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-33 to R-LIT-35 and R-LIT-41 to R-LIT-43; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T3.2, T4; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R5.5
section: RWB-S4-E5011-APP sections 2, 3, 4 (step 5), 8 (BR4), 12.2, 12.8, 13, 18, 19; RWB-S4-E5011-CON sections 2, 3, 7 (AC5), 8 (BR6), 12.2, 12.8, 19; the patterns rows of both story files and the two fragments
description: The step evaluates six LITIGATION rules at the version in force and reads two closed vocabularies, but the pattern set of this key is DP03, DP13 and DP19 only. DP-04 (embedded Drools with rule packages from rwb-decision) is not applied, so no rule-package contract appears in the H, C or I rows; DP-06 and DP-07 (parameters and reference data of rwb-case) are not applied either, so the two LOV vocabularies and the deadline values have no owner row. The host of the evaluation is therefore a design statement with no dependency behind it, and the rule rows and LOV values reach the service on contracts the metadata does not name.
evidence: Context pack short DP table: DP-03, DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07 each add a platform H row and a C row to the owning service contract. The WP legacy record carries 'patterns': ['DP03', 'DP13', 'DP19'] and 'H': ['RWB-S4-E5011-CON', 'RWB-PLT-E1027-CON', 'RWB-PLT-N001-CON'], with C, I and X empty. TSD S4 T3.2 gives LOV-HEARING and LOV-HEARING-OUTCOME with no owner; T4 gives 79 rules over 38 states in the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook.
area: Rules and reference data, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision and P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P7 rwb-decision and P3 rwb-case architects
proposed: Name the rule package read of rwb-decision and the reference-data ride of rwb-case on the contract rows of 12.2, leave the H, C and I metadata rows exactly as the plan gives them, and record that the dependency rows for DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07 are added centrally if the plan is revised.

title: The trigger of the step is named by no source, the legacy endpoints name no hearing operation, and the case answer has no operation name
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-011 endpoints table and AC1 'When its trigger arrives'); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.11.2 and A2.11.4.4 (system background events None); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T-A.1 and T5.2; _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows)
description: Three readings collide. (1) The trigger: the legacy story says the step is a System step that runs when 'its trigger arrives', while FSD S4 A2.11.4.4 declares no system background event and the ownership rows give the service zero events, so the arrival is a workflow signal with no publisher. (2) The surface: the legacy endpoints table names only the legal-action create and the legal-action read, while the hearing operation of the step is API-S4-005 of TSD T-A.1, which the legacy table does not carry. (3) The case answer: the move, the case timer and the officer task that the step raises have no operation name in any source; T5.2 says only 'P3 for the case'.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.11.4.4: 'None | No background event'. Legacy endpoints: 'POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions' and 'GET /api/recovery/v1/legal-actions/{legalActionId}' only. TSD S4 T-A.1: API-S4-005 'POST /api/recovery/v1/legal-actions/{legalActionId}/hearings', first in E5. TSD S4 T5.2: 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data'. Context pack: 'Events (0)', 'REST operations provided (5)'.
area: Integration and trigger design, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case and S9 rwb-partner
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case, S9 rwb-partner architects and the event platform team
proposed: Read the trigger as a signal of `LitigationWorkflow` raised on the officer's hearing request or on the firm's court-date entry, not as a Kafka subscription; name the hearing operation of TSD T-A.1 as the provided surface of the step and the legal-action create as the sibling story's; carry the case read and the case stage answer on the rwb-case contract with the placeholder, and declare no event in 12.3 or 12.4.

title: No requirement identifier, hearing lead time, spend limit or prescription horizon is given for this key
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T8 (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 all mapped to FEAT-LIT-01); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.11.3.1; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-011)
section: RWB-S4-E5011-APP sections 2, 3, 7 (AC1), 8 (BR6), 11, 13, 18; RWB-S4-E5011-CON sections 3, 7 (AC1), 8 (BR1), 11, 18; the reqs keys of both fragments
description: The legacy master carries no requirement ID for RWB-E5-011, TSD S4 T8 lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 against FEAT-LIT-01 only, and the FSD A2.11.3.1 carries VR-S4-011-1 and BR-S4-011 with no requirement row. The same gap covers three values the step needs and no source gives: the hearing lead time that a deadline measures, the D7.4 spend limit that R-LIT-41 and R-LIT-42 route against, and the 90-day prescription warning that the Temporal slide names. All three are business values held by reference or rule rows, so none may be invented here.
evidence: TSD S4 T8: ten rows, all 'FEAT-LIT-01', story 'Written one epic ahead'. FSD S4 A2.11.3.1: 'VR-S4-011-1 Data product stale ...' and 'BR-S4-011 No value a business person may change is written in code'. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-41 and R-LIT-42 name 'the D7.4 limit' with no number; context pack slide 7 notes name '90 days or less' as the escalation horizon.
area: Requirements and reference data, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst, S4, with the PRD builder and the reference-data owner of rwb-case
proposed: Trace both stories to FEAT-LIT-11 until the PRD allocates requirement IDs, carry the hearing lead time, the D7.4 spend limit and the prescription horizon as versioned reference or rule rows, and keep the placeholder on every place a value would otherwise be fixed.
